segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now concerning the things of the Spirit, brothers and sisters, I do not want you to be uninformed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You know that when you were Gentiles, you were carried off to idols that cannot speak, however you happened to be led.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So I make it known to you that no one speaking by the Spirit of God says,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Jesus is accursed,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and no one can say,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Jesus is Lord,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: except by the Holy Spirit.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now there are different allotments of gifts, but the same Spirit;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and there are different allotments of service, and the same Lord;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and there are different allotments of workings, but the same God, who works all of them in everyone.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: To each one the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common good.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For to one a word of wisdom is given through the Spirit, to another a word of knowledge according to the same Spirit,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by the one Spirit,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: to another workings of miracles, to another prophecy, to another the distinguishing of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But one and the same Spirit works all these things, allotting to each one individually just as he determines.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For just as the body is one and has many parts, and all the parts of the body, though many, are one body, so it is with Christ.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether slaves or free, and we were all given one Spirit to drink.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For indeed the body is not one part but many.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: If the foot were to say,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: it would not for that reason cease to belong to the body.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And if the ear were to say,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: it would not for that reason cease to belong to the body.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the sense of smell be?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But as it is, God placed the parts in the body, each one of them, just as he wished.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: If they were all one part, where would the body be?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But as it is, there are many parts, yet one body.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The eye cannot say to the hand,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I have no need of you,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: nor again the head to the feet,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I have no need of you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are all the more necessary,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and those parts of the body that we think less honorable we clothe with greater honor, and our unpresentable parts are made all the more presentable,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: while our presentable parts have no such need. But God has blended the body together, giving greater honor to the part that lacks it,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: so that there may be no division in the body, but the parts may have the same concern for one another.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And if one part suffers, all the parts suffer with it; if one part is honored, all the parts rejoice with it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you a part of it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And God placed in the assembly first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healing, acts of assistance, acts of guidance, kinds of tongues.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But be eager for the greater gifts. And further, I will show you a way beyond comparison.

notes.note: The Greek is simply 'the spiritual [things or persons]'; the word 'gifts' is not there, and Paul uses a different word for 'gifts' from verse 4 on. The form could also be masculine, 'spiritual people'. Most translations supply 'gifts' from the context, which is a reasonable inference; the rendering here leaves the phrase as open as the Greek.

The Greek plural is grammatically masculine but was the ordinary way to address a mixed group of men and women, as the Corinthian community plainly was. Some translations keep 'brothers' as more literal; many recent ones render as here.

This is the same Greek word translated 'nations' elsewhere; in the plural it regularly means the non-Jewish peoples. Paul says 'when you were Gentiles', as though his largely non-Jewish readers no longer belong to that category. Many modern versions say 'pagans' here to bring out the religious sense.

In the Greek Old Testament this word is used for something handed over to God for destruction, and so for a person under God's curse. 'Jesus is Lord' is the basic confession of the early communities. Whether anyone in Corinth actually said 'Jesus is accursed', and in what setting, is debated; Paul may be stating an extreme case to make his point.

The noun can mean either 'distribution, apportioning' or 'difference, variety', and standard lexicons allow both here. 'Allotments' is chosen because verse 11 closes the paragraph with the matching verb: the Spirit 'allotting' to each one. Most translations have 'varieties' in verses 4–6, which loses that link.

The Greek word is the ordinary one for the tongue and for a language. 'Tongues' is kept as the established term for the Spirit-prompted speech Paul discusses at length in chapter 14, but a first-century reader would simply have heard 'kinds of languages'. What kind of speech this was, and how it relates to the languages of Acts 2, is disputed.

The word means a limb or organ of the body. 'Member' once meant exactly that, but a modern reader hears it as belonging to a club or congregation, a sense that actually derives from this passage. 'Parts' keeps the bodily picture; several modern translations do the same.

notes.traditional: by one Spirit / in one Spirit
notes.note: The preposition can mean 'in' (the Spirit as the element in which believers are baptized) or 'by' (the Spirit as the one who baptizes). Translations are divided. 'In' matches the Gospels' phrase 'baptize in the Holy Spirit' and the image of drinking that follows; the same preposition is rendered 'by' in verses 3 and 9, where agency is the natural sense.

The Greek word was the everyday term for a civic gathering and the Greek Old Testament's word for Israel assembled before God. 'Church' is the near-universal rendering and readers know what it refers to, but it now suggests a building or an institution. This translation uses 'assembly' throughout so that the reader can see it is one word.

The word is literally the steering of a ship; in the Greek book of Proverbs it is used for wise direction or counsel. It occurs only here in the New Testament. Whether Paul means leadership of the community or the giving of sound guidance more generally is uncertain; translations vary between 'administration', 'leadership' and 'guidance'.

The Greek form can be a command ('be eager for') or a statement ('you are eager for'). Most translations take it as a command, as in 14:1, where the same verb is clearly an instruction. A minority read it as a mild rebuke: 'you are eager for the greater gifts, but I will show you a better way.'

candidates.reason: The plural address occurs throughout the letters and Acts, and translations split between 'brothers' and 'brothers and sisters'; it should not vary chapter to chapter.
'Tongues' versus 'languages' needs one decision across Acts 2, 10, 19 and 1 Corinthians 12–14, since varying it would suggest different phenomena.
The body image recurs in Romans 6 and 12, 1 Corinthians 6, Ephesians and Colossians, and 'members' versus 'parts' should be uniform.
Recurs in Romans, 1 Corinthians, the Pastorals and 1 Peter, where 'gift', 'spiritual gift' and 'gift of grace' compete and its link to χάρις may warrant a consistent choice.
In the plural sense of acts of power it recurs across the Gospels, Acts and the letters, where 'miracles', 'mighty works' and 'deeds of power' compete.
